papers.title: Spin-Phonon Relaxation and Decoherence in a Three-Dimensional Paired-Ion Framework Composed of Vanadyl Porphyrin Qubits
papers.authors: Christian A. Epure, Georgia C. Mantel, Casandra M. Moisanu, Jonathan R. Palmer, Madison I. Bardot, Michael R. Wasielewski, William R. Dichtel
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: An ionic three-dimensional framework positions vanadyl porphyrin spins in a dense array. EPR measurements associate the short coherence times with dipolar interactions, while spin–lattice relaxation remains similar to dilute porphyrin solutions.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful comparison for separating spin-density effects from lattice-driven relaxation in molecular qubit frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how a framework environment influences spin–lattice relaxation.
Offers a comparison between dense spin arrays and spatial isolation of molecular qubits.

papers.title: Multireference Density Matrix Embedding for Spin-Phonon Relaxation
papers.authors: Shreya Verma, Antonio L. Mariano, Matthew R. Hermes, Alessandro Lunghi, Giulia Galli, Laura Gagliardi
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: A multireference embedding approach computes spin–phonon relaxation while treating a restricted region at the expensive electronic-structure level. Tests on molecular magnets and a molecular crystal suggest a route to lower-cost relaxation calculations.
papers.whyRelevant: Could help make crystal-level spin–phonon modeling more tractable; transfer to Sunlab materials would need separate validation.

relatedPapers.reason: Connects computational treatment of spin–phonon interactions to molecular qubit frameworks.
Provides another theoretical approach to spin–lattice relaxation.

papers.title: Investigation of Magnetic Properties in Exchange Coupled Radical-Nickelocene Complexes by Adopting a Generalized Spin Hamiltonian
papers.authors: Abhishek R. Nath, Md. Ehesan Ali
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: Calculations of radical–nickelocene complexes show why a simple exchange model can miss the interplay between local anisotropy and coupled spin states. An expanded effective Hamiltonian resolves zero-field splitting and anisotropic exchange contributions.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant when interpreting interactions between radical qubits and anisotropic coordination environments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern coupled radical-based molecular architectures; their materials and methods differ.

papers.title: Optimal‐Control 19 F PROJECT Improves the Reliability of CPMG‐Derived Relaxation Rates
papers.authors: Marco Schiavina, Enrico Luchinat, Enrico Ravera
papers.summary: Optimal-control pulses combined with the PROJECT echo sequence reduce scalar-coupling bias in fluorine NMR relaxation estimates. The comparison with CPMG also identifies a signal-to-noise limit below which neither method gives reliable rates.
papers.whyRelevant: A concrete example of distinguishing pulse-sequence artifacts from genuine relaxation, with potential methodological lessons for spin experiments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address errors associated with spin-control or decoupling protocols.
Provides a comparison for separating measurement artifacts from sensing signals.

papers.title: Ten-second electron-spin coherence in isotopically engineered diamond
papers.authors: Takashi Yamamoto, Hendrik Benjamin van Ommen, Kai-Niklas Schymik, Beer de Zoeten, Shinobu Onoda, Seiichi Saiki, Takeshi Ohshima, Hadi Arjmandi-Tash, René Vollmer, Tim Hugo Taminiau
papers.summary: Isotopically engineered diamond, real-time compensation of power-line noise and tailored decoupling extend NV electron-spin coherence to about eleven seconds. The work also characterizes optical coherence and spectral diffusion.
papers.whyRelevant: Helps distinguish improvements from material purification, environmental noise suppression and pulse control; the platform differs from molecular qubits.

relatedPapers.reason: Dynamical decoupling and its practical limitations are shared methodological themes.
Both connect spin coherence with optical properties relevant to quantum technologies.

papers.title: Electron spin resonance in scanning probe microscopy: From single‐spin spectroscopy to atomically engineered quantum operations
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how scanning-probe techniques bring ESR spectroscopy and coherent manipulation to individual surface spins. It discusses electrical and force-based detection routes and the construction of locally engineered spin systems.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful orientation for connecting molecular-spin control with atomically resolved surface experiments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address coherent control at the level of individual molecular electron spins.
Connects surface assembly and local structural control to possible spin-based measurements.

papers.title: Electron–Nuclear Hyperfine Coupling Enables Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Detection of Diamagnetic Cu(I) with Trityl Spin Probes
papers.authors: Yan Wang, Xiaoli Tan, Jing Zhao, Qi Chang, Yuqi Hu, Hui Gao, Wenbin Cai, Yafei Wang, Yuguang Song, Yangping Liu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Trityl radicals attached to copper-selective ligands convert binding of normally EPR-silent Cu(I) into a resolved hyperfine signature. The study reports selective detection and applications to biological copper measurements.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to coupling chemical recognition with spin readout for detecting otherwise difficult-to-observe ions.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use recognition chemistry to translate ion binding into a spin-sensitive signal.

papers.title: Multiple quantum 19 F electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) for distance measurements with multifluorinated spin probes
papers.authors: Sergei Kuzin, Lucca Sielaff, Karoline Goldschmidt, Marina Bennati
papers.summary: Time-domain ENDOR with multiple fluorine nuclei reveals multiple-quantum coherences and nuclear dipolar couplings. The framework extends the structural information available from electron–nuclear distances to relationships between nearby nuclei.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a magnetic-resonance route to characterize local molecular geometry around spin probes.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use molecular spins to probe local surroundings, although the observables differ.
Nuclear couplings are relevant context for manipulating molecular electron spins.

papers.title: Nonlinear collective-spin dynamics for quantum-enhanced sensing in solid-state platforms
papers.summary: This tutorial explains how nonlinear collective-spin interactions can create squeezed or entangled states for improved sensing. It relates ideal dynamics to disorder, decoherence and experimental control in solid-state systems.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides a broader framework for evaluating whether interactions in spin ensembles could benefit sensing instead of only limiting coherence.

relatedPapers.reason: Offers complementary context for the relationship between control protocols and sensing performance.

papers.title: Photoinduced Electron Transfer in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Keegan L. Everitt, Kiran Avinash, Aldan R. Dye, William C. Clifford II, Gabriel J. Streblow, Amarthya Chalasani, Sheeza Fatima, Aanuoluwapo E. Adeniyi, Halley Le, Justin L. Andrews
papers.summary: A functional ligand couples ionic and electronic behavior in a conductive two-dimensional copper framework. The reported optical and electronic responses survive framework formation, enabling externally modulated conductance.
papers.whyRelevant: A close match to studying how ligand design and external conditions alter transport in conductive MOFs.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine changes in measurable conductivity under external influences.
Fits the broader connection between framework structure and emergent electronic properties.

papers.title: Solution-Processed Ultrathin Cu-TCPP Metal−Organic Framework Films for Self-Powered Organic Photodetectors
papers.summary: Spin-coating a coordination precursor followed by thermal treatment produces continuous ultrathin Cu-TCPP films. Incorporating the films into organic photodetectors suppresses dark current and changes photoresponse, linking processing conditions to device behavior.
papers.whyRelevant: A practical comparison for MOF film integration, morphology control and contact-sensitive device measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect MOF morphology with electronic-device fabrication.
Provides a contrasting solution-processing route to the lab’s dry fabrication approach.

papers.title: Localized Plasmon-Induced Bond Dissociation in a Two-Dimensional Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Naoki Hashimoto, Toyo Kazu Yamada, Masaki Horie, Adnan Hammud, Martin Wolf, Akitoshi Shiotari
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Combined STM and tip-enhanced Raman measurements resolve local plasmon-driven reactions in a surface-supported two-dimensional MOF. Cobalt coordination reduces molecular bond cleavage, enabling less destructive nanoscale spectroscopic observation.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to interpreting whether local optical probes alter the structures and interfaces they measure.

relatedPapers.reason: Both study surface-supported frameworks in which the substrate and local environment matter.
Connects coordination-bond stability with atomically resolved surface structures.

papers.title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
papers.authors: Fan Zhou, Qing Hao, Youxian Li, Panke Zhou, Bingbing Gao, Qiongfeng Shi, Dong Wang, Hong Liu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A template-assisted melt-pressing strategy creates crystalline inverse-opal COF architectures. The quasi-solid precursor combines template infiltration with continued framework formation, offering control over macroporosity and optical structure across several linkage chemistries.
papers.whyRelevant: Suggests a synthesis strategy for coordinating crystallization with larger-scale architecture rather than optimizing crystallinity alone.

relatedPapers.reason: Both tackle the relationship between reaction conditions and framework crystallization.
Offers complementary control over structure across length scales.

papers.title: Optimizing the synthesis of imine-linked covalent organic frameworks for high surface areas
papers.summary: A comparison of imine-linked COF synthesis protocols finds that a simple open-reflux route can achieve high surface area without degassing. A more elaborate procedure provides only a modest further improvement in the model system.
papers.whyRelevant: Useful for evaluating which synthesis steps improve reproducibility and porosity before adding experimental complexity.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how synthesis choices govern the quality of framework materials.

papers.title: Flexible Nickel-Fumarate Metal–Organic Framework Exhibiting Reversible Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Phase Transformation for Adsorptive Separation of Water–Organic Azeotropic Mixtures
papers.authors: Yi Cheng, Bochun Zhang, Qingqing Yan, Yafei Du, Shuyi An, Xiaohe Miao, Sujing Wang
papers.summary: A nickel–fumarate MOF undergoes reversible structural reorganization during activation and rehydration while retaining single-crystal character. Its water-specific recovery creates selective adsorption behavior through changes in coordination and pore geometry.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful structural comparison for frameworks exposed to humidity or other environmental stimuli during measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect framework–water interactions to measurable behavior; sensing and separation are distinct applications.
Provides structural context for interpreting moisture-dependent responses in MOFs.
